summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute facial and neck tremors and hypoxemia following a recent fall and ongoing treatment with ciprofloxacin for a multidrug-resistant UTI. The tremors were attributed to a likely adverse effect of ciprofloxacin, possibly exacerbated by new pneumonia and aspiration. A head CT showed no acute intracranial process, and an EEG revealed no seizure activity, though there was right frontocentral slowing. He was treated with intravenous Zosyn for pneumonia, which was later transitioned to oral clindamycin. The tremors resolved after discontinuation of ciprofloxacin and initiation of clonazepam. His oxygen levels improved with supplemental oxygen, which was weaned successfully. He was discharged back to his rehab facility in stable condition with follow-up planned in neurology and urology clinics.
